questions.q: Why parameterize a value like a resource group name with a variable instead of hardcoding it?
options: So the same configuration file can provision dev, staging, and production just by changing the variable's value, without copying the file
Because Terraform refuses to accept hardcoded string values in resource blocks
Hardcoding and variables produce identical behavior with no practical difference
Because variables are required for every single attribute, even ones that never change
questions.explain: A variable lets one configuration serve multiple environments safely, avoiding the copy-paste risk of duplicating files per environment.

questions.q: What does a `variable` block's `default` field do?
options: Forces that value to be used no matter what is passed at apply time
Supplies the value Terraform uses when no other value is explicitly provided
Deletes the variable if left unset
Declares the variable's data type
questions.explain: If default is omitted, Terraform requires the value to be supplied explicitly; if present, it's the fallback value.

questions.q: How do you reference a declared variable inside a resource block?
options: $<variable name>
var.<variable name>
resource.<variable name>
output.<variable name>
questions.explain: var.<name> is Terraform's syntax for substituting a variable's value anywhere inside a configuration.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an `output` block?
options: To delete a resource after it's created
To document a resource block's description only
To print a named value after apply finishes, so it can be read without digging through the state file by hand
To declare an input variable's default value
questions.explain: Outputs surface a resource's attribute (like its Azure resource ID) as a result other tools or configurations can consume.

questions.q: What is the most common way real teams apply the same configuration to different environments using variables?
options: Editing the default value in the variable block before every apply
A separate .tfvars file per environment (e.g. dev.tfvars, staging.tfvars), applied with -var-file
Manually copying the entire .tf file for each environment
Running terraform apply with no variables at all
questions.explain: A per-environment .tfvars file keeps the configuration itself identical while only the supplied values differ.
